The percentage error in measurement of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>b</mi></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>c</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi></math> are<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>%</mo></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>%</mo></math>, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>%</mo></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>%</mo></math> respectively.
questions.solution:
Percentage error in A

=2Δaa+3Δbb+12Δcc+Δdd

=2×1+3×3+12×2+1×1%=13%

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A student measures the distance covered and time taken by a body under free fall which was initially at rest. He uses this data for estimating <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math>, the acceleration due to gravity. If the maximum percentage errors in measurement of the distance and the time are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> respectively, then the maximum possible percentage error in the estimation of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> is
questions.solution:
From the relation

h = ut + 1 2 gt 2

h = 1 2 gt 2 ⇒ g = 2 h t 2 ∵ body initially at rest

Taking natural logarithms on both sides, we get

lng=lnh-2lnt+ln2

Differentiating, Δ g g = Δ h h - 2 Δ t t

For maximum permissible errors, we add both the errors. So

Δgg×100max=Δhh×100+2×Δtt×100

Δ h h × 100 = e 1 and Δ t t × 100 = e 2

Therefore, Δ g g × 100 max =  e 1 + 2 e 2

questions.q: A professor reads a greeting card received on his 50th birthday with + 2.5 D glasses keeping the card 25 cm away. Ten years letter, he reads his farewell letter with the same glasses but he has to keep the letter 50 cm away. What should be the power (in dioptre) of the lens now so that he can keep the letter at the same distance as ten years ago?
questions.solution:
Firstly find out distance of retina from his eye lens i.e., image distance in first case (we are assuming distance between eye lens and retina is not changing which is not true practically we are taking that liberty to make problem more mathematically convenient. However it doesn't effect base line of problem)

1 v - 1 - 2 5 = 1 f⁡ 1

1 v + 1 2 5 = 1 f⁡ 1

for second case image distance should be same

1 v + 1 5 0 = 1 f⁡ 2

⇒ 1 2 5 - 1 5 0 = 1 f⁡ 1 - 1 f⁡ 2

⇒ 1 cm - 1 5 0 = 1 f⁡ 1 - 1 f⁡ 2 = P 1 - P 2 = 2  D

Let power of his eye lens in two cases are (Pe)1, (Pe)2 respectively

P 1 = 2.5 + P e 1

P 2 = 2.5 + P e 2

⇒ P 1 - P 2 = P e 1 - P e 2

          = 2 D

So loss in power is 2 D so he should use additional power of 2 D i.e. 4.5 D
